docs.when: Small MVPs, student projects, prototypes, simple CRUD
docs.not_when: Complex business logic, multi-year lifespans, deep domain testing independent of frameworks
docs.title: PROFILE: SIMPLE LAYERED ARCHITECTURE

when_to_choose: Solo developer or small team, lightweight business logic, rapid prototype delivery required.
Primarily CRUD data access; zero need to decouple database or framework.
when_not_to_choose: Complex business rules requiring framework-independent domain unit tests: use clean-architecture.md.
Multiple independent features developed in parallel: use vertical-slice.md.
constraints: Dependency flow: `routes → services → data`. Reverse direction is strictly prohibited; `routes` never query the DB directly.
`lib/` and `config/` are shared helpers and must not depend on the three layers above.
Guardrail Level M1 (see ../README.md): Working lint + test + build running in CI.
adding_a_feature: Record objective and acceptance criteria in `tasks/task-spec.md`.
Write unit tests for `services` (1 happy path + 2 edge/failure cases).
Implement business logic function in `services`, accessing storage via `data`.
Create a thin route handler calling the service; validate inputs at the route layer.
Run test/lint/build verification commands; update `docs/project-brief.md` if user journeys change.
common_mistakes: Route layer containing direct SQL/ORM queries or complex calculations (layer leakage).
Monolithic god-files > 350 lines combining UI, state, and database queries.
Swallowing errors silently; bare `JSON.parse` without error handling.

docs.when: Complex business logic, framework-independent domain models, long-term evolvability
docs.not_when: Small demos, simple CRUD, solo prototypes with minimal business logic
docs.title: PROFILE: CLEAN ARCHITECTURE (+ OPTIONAL DDD)

when_to_choose: Rich enterprise business rules requiring consistent invariants across a long product lifecycle.
Need to execute high-speed unit tests on core business logic without spinning up databases or HTTP web servers.
Infrastructure volatility (anticipating swaps of database, cloud providers, or UI frameworks).
when_not_to_choose: Demos, prototypes, simple CRUD: use simple-layered.md; DTO and interface boilerplate exceeds benefits.
Systems best structured around independent feature workflows: use vertical-slice.md.
constraints: Dependency Rule: All dependencies point inward. `Domain` must not import anything from outer layers or external frameworks. `Application` depends only on `Domain` and its own declared interfaces.
`Domain`/`Application` defines repository interfaces; `Infrastructure` provides concrete implementations. Wire dependencies via Dependency Injection (DI) at a single Composition Root.
Enforce domain invariants and state mutations inside rich entities (avoid anemic data bags).
Guardrail Level M2 (see ../README.md): Enforce package boundaries or linting rules prohibiting inward dependency leaks.
adding_a_feature: Domain: Define or extend entities, value objects, domain events, and core invariants.
Application: Implement the use case and declare necessary repository/gateway interfaces.
Infrastructure: Implement repository interfaces against database or external APIs.
Presentation: Expose a thin HTTP endpoint that dispatches directly to the use case.
Automated Testing: Write domain and use case unit tests first (no database fixtures needed).
common_mistakes: Controllers or routes querying the database directly (`ARCH-001`).
`Domain` importing ORM libraries, database drivers, or HTTP clients.
Anemic entities (getters/setters only) with procedural business logic leaked into services.
Missing composition root; ad-hoc DI registration scattered across the codebase.

docs.when: Systems with multiple independent, feature-sliced capabilities developed in parallel
docs.not_when: Features share heavily coupled core entities and strict transactional invariants
docs.title: PROFILE: VERTICAL SLICE ARCHITECTURE (FEATURE-BASED)

when_to_choose: Multiple relatively independent features; goal is to add or modify a feature without touching other features.
Small team or multiple parallel AI agents collaborating on different features concurrently.
when_not_to_choose: Features share heavily coupled domain models and business invariants: use clean-architecture.md or modular-monolith.md.
Very small, single-purpose projects: simple-layered.md is sufficient.
constraints: Slices never import other feature slices. If duplication occurs, extract to `shared/` only after 2–3 real use cases emerge (rule of three, avoid premature abstraction).
`shared/` must never depend on `features/` and must never host feature-specific business rules.
Guardrail Level M2 (see ../README.md): Enforce lint rules prohibiting cross-feature imports between `features/*` folders.
adding_a_feature: Write vertical slice tests first (from handler invocation to mocked or isolated persistence).
Register the new feature handler in `app.*` router.
common_mistakes: One feature directly importing types or handlers from another feature slice.
`shared/` degenerating into a catch-all dumping ground containing feature-specific logic.
Inconsistent error handling or logging across slices due to missing `shared/` conventions.

docs.when: Monolithic systems growing in scale requiring strict bounded contexts and module boundaries
docs.not_when: Small projects with few domains; or systems already requiring independent container deployment per service
docs.title: PROFILE: MODULAR MONOLITH

when_to_choose: System scope is growing and requires explicit module boundaries for task parallelization (humans or AI agents), but single-deployment operational simplicity is preferred.
Internal architecture can leverage Clean Architecture or Vertical Slice inside each individual module.
when_not_to_choose: Small projects with single simple domains: use simple-layered.md or vertical-slice.md.
Strict operational requirements for independent scaling/deployment per service: requires microservices ADR and explicit user consultation.
constraints: Modules interact with other modules exclusively via Public API contracts (interfaces, DTOs, or domain events). Direct import of another module's internal files is strictly prohibited.
Database tables must not be shared directly across module boundaries (access via module APIs).
`shared/` must never contain domain business logic.
Guardrail Level M3 (see ../README.md): Enforce package boundaries or lint rules prohibiting private internal imports; ADR required for boundary changes.
adding_a_feature: Identify the owning domain module. If new, create module and register it in `specs/domains.md`.
Implement feature logic entirely inside that module.
If data from another module is needed: expose a method via that module's Public API, never bypass via internal imports.
common_mistakes: Cross-importing private internal directories of foreign modules.
Monolithic god-modules conflating multiple distinct business subdomains.
